C-01.1.answer: The new detector counts a range-topology run that reports no tests at all as a failure, never as a killed mutant; a drill anchor missing from its file is DRILL BROKEN, and the two push-hook mutants plant exactly the absence of a refusal.
C-01.1.guard: test/core-specs.test.mjs::every drill anchor is found exactly once in its file, without running the drill (F-149)

C-01.2.answer: Deleting the every-parent merge test turns the detector red, because the planted first-parent-only checker then survives the range tests; deleting one of the new run_drill lines breaks the EXPECTED_MUTANTS tripwire.
C-01.2.guard: test/certificate.test.mjs::EXPECTED_MUTANTS equals the number the drill actually defines

C-02.1.answer: The four new mutants are a chosen sample of the range rules, as mutation testing samples by design; the drill list is counted against EXPECTED_MUTANTS, not claimed complete, and the PR body names the range rules still without a planted bug.
C-02.1.guard: test/certificate.test.mjs::every mutant the drill defines is counted exactly once

C-02.2.answer: The same gap applies to every rule of the range check and the push hook. Planted here: every-parent compare, the removal refusal, the range result and the suite result. The inherited-copy, rename and base-file rules stay test-only and are listed as remaining.
C-02.2.guard: test/range-topology.test.mjs::an answers file already on the base may not be removed or rewritten

C-03.1.answer: Each mutant was applied by hand on a copy before it went into the drill, and its named test was seen red; the first-parent-only mutant was first seen to survive every existing test (finding F-221) and is now killed by the new merge test alone.
C-03.1.guard: test/range-every-parent-detector.test.mjs::the range tests go red when the checker compares a merge commit with its first parent only (F-221)

C-03.2.answer: The reworded answer sits only on the merge commit's second parent, so a checker that compares only the first parent cannot see it; the control merges the same line without rewording and must pass, so the red comes from the rewrite.
C-03.2.guard: test/range-topology.test.mjs::a merge commit is compared with every parent: rewording an answer that came only from its second parent is refused

C-03.3.answer: The docs' sentence that a merge commit is compared with both sides is now tied to a test that runs the real checker on a real merge, and each drill verdict carries the mutated file's hashes, which the certificate checks for freshness.
C-03.3.guard: test/certificate.test.mjs::the freshness parser can see every mutant id the drill emits (the MUT-AA regex gap)

C-04.1.answer: Four mutants take the drill to 44 of the 45 its 30-minute job allows under the per-mutant budget, each running only its guardian files; the detector runs the range-topology file twice under a fixed spawn timeout, bounded by count, not a stopwatch assertion.
C-04.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::the drill job has time for every mutant it runs (F-166)

C-05.1.answer: The added retarget sentence says a retargeted child is asked only about its own files however its parent was merged; the parent-merged-first test now runs plain merge, rebase and squash, and fails if any of them asks about the parent's files.
C-05.1.guard: test/range-topology.test.mjs::a child whose parent was merged, rebase-merged or squash-merged into main is not asked about the parent's files

C-05.2.answer: EXPECTED_MUTANTS goes to 44 and its comment now names MUT-A to MUT-AR; the certificate test compares the figure with the drill's real run_drill count, and the drill exits non-zero on any survivor, wrong killer or broken anchor.
C-05.2.guard: test/certificate.test.mjs::every mutant the drill defines is counted exactly once

C-06.1.answer: The claim that the range rules are guarded rests on mutants applied and seen red in guardian files, plus the detector's own run, not on test names; the F-221 evidence is the run where the first-parent mutant passed every range test.
C-06.1.guard: test/drill-runs-guardians-only.test.mjs::the drill runs a mutant against the files holding its named test, not the whole suite

C-07.1.answer: The only inputs are repository history and answers files that the tests build in throwaway repositories; the checker already treats each answers file as untrusted and compares it with every parent. Nothing from an outside party is newly read.
C-07.1.guard: test/range-topology.test.mjs::two lines developed in parallel and merged are each compared with their own parents

C-07.2.answer: No new gate constrains an agent here: the mutants live in the drill and the detector is a test, and a raised EXPECTED_MUTANTS must still equal the drill's real count, which an agent cannot satisfy without adding a real mutant.
C-07.2.guard: none: this change adds tests and planted bugs, and no gate a person must clear

C-09.1.answer: The detector copies the range test and the gate's files into a temp folder outside any repository and strips the GIT_ and node test runner variables, so it behaves the same under npm test, the pre-push hook and the guard proof.
C-09.1.guard: test/range-every-parent-detector.test.mjs::an unmutated copy of the checker keeps the range tests green (control)

C-09.2.answer: The mutants run in CI's drill job through scripts/mutation-drill.sh, the same script the audit and the certificate call; I run the drill locally on this branch for the four new ids and read each verdict line before pushing.
C-09.2.guard: test/drill-guardians.test.mjs::every mutant's named test is found in a file its suite runs

C-10.1.answer: That each range rule fails when broken was only a doc sentence; now a planted bug in four of those rules must die red in the drill, and the count of planted bugs is tied to the gate certificate's tripwire.
C-10.1.guard: test/certificate.test.mjs::the freshness parser can see every mutant id the drill emits (the MUT-AA regex gap)

C-10.2.answer: The push-hook mutants plant a hook that ignores the range result or the suite result, and the test that kills them drives the real hook. A pull request retarget is no new route: CI runs again against the new base, a shape the tests cover.
C-10.2.guard: test/pre-push.test.mjs::a push runs the range check and the full suite, and refuses when either fails

C-13.1.answer: Both sides are measured: a merge rewording a second-parent answer is refused while the same merge unchanged passes, and the detector sees the mutated checker go red while an unmutated copy of the checker stays green.
C-13.1.guard: test/range-every-parent-detector.test.mjs::the range tests go red when the checker compares a merge commit with its first parent only (F-221)

C-14.1.answer: Each mutant runs in its own temporary copy, so a broken one is DRILL BROKEN under its own id while the others carry on; the detector removes its temp copy in a finally block, red or green.
C-14.1.guard: test/drill-guardians.test.mjs::a named test found in no file refuses, and a suite without one glob refuses
